subject: Renewal: commit recalibration, invoice timing & one-time credits
messages:
From: Priya Singh <procurement@heliocharge.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: ben@heliocharge.com
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal negotiation: commit recalibration + invoice timing

Hi Grace,

Hope you’re well. We’re working toward budget signoff for our Redwood renewal and have a couple of asks from procurement and finance before we route for executive approval.

Quick summary of our position: we’d like to keep the same committed GPU-hr band but recalibrate the true-up cadence to align with our fiscal year (starts 2028-07-01). Concretely: 1) a one-time bridge credit to cover projected Q3 overages, 2) a short-term price hold for 6 months post-renewal, and 3) invoice date aligned to 2028-07-01 (our AP window).

Attached is our usage export for Q4 2027 that shows the spike patterns we’re worried about. We can consider signing a 12-month commit with a 10% uplift if we get the bridge credit and invoice timing.

Questions for you: what flexibility do you have on invoice date and can you put the price-hold and bridge credit into the MSA addendum (or SOW)? Also our Exec prefers one-time onboarding/transition credits rather than ongoing discounts.

Can Marissa or your pricing team advise on a proposed package we can take to our CFO? CC’ing Ben (product) in case there are technical constraints around usage smoothing.

Thanks,
Priya
Procurement | HelioCharge

Attachment: HelioCharge_usage_Q4_2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: Priya Singh <procurement@heliocharge.com>
Cc: ben@heliocharge.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: commit recalibration + invoice timing

Priya —

Thanks for the data and clear ask. Appreciate the heads-up on the fiscal cadence. We’re open to a couple of mechanisms that address HelioCharge’s goals while keeping unit economics intact for both sides. High level options we can pull together quickly:

- Option A (preferred for predictability): 12-month commit at the same list rate, a one-time bridge credit equal to 8% of the first-quarter expected spend (applied as invoice credit), and a 6-month price-hold (no price increases). Invoice issue date moved to 2028-07-01 for the first renewal invoice; subsequent invoices follow monthly cadence.

- Option B (preferred by finance for cash): 10% upfront discount on the first invoice in exchange for keeping standard calendar invoicing. No bridge credit, but we’ll include a usage-smoothing clause (automatic burst credits for unexpected spikes up to a bounded cap).

I’m looping in Marissa for the exact numbers and Karthik to confirm the commit/true-up language and SLA credit triggers. If leadership wants one-time onboarding credit rather than a percent discount, we can replace the 8% bridge with a fixed onboarding credit (e.g., $45k) — happy to present both figures.

Next steps: Marissa, can you produce a short table with Option A & B numbers + suggested SOW language? Karthik, can you confirm we can change invoice first-issue date to 2028-07-01 and how that impacts revenue recognition?

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0199

—

Priya / Grace —

Attached is a short worksheet and an updated SOW (v2) that implements the two options Grace outlined. Numbers are illustrative; happy to finalize once we have confirmation on the preferred credit structure.

Summary (short):
- Option A: 12-mo commit; 6-mo price-hold; bridge credit = 8% of first-quarter forecast (~$52,000); invoice aligned to 2028-07-01 for first invoice; standard monthly thereafter.
- Option B: 12-mo commit; 10% discount applied to first invoice only; no bridge credit; standard invoice date.

SLA / credits: we propose explicit SLA credit triggers (latency/availability thresholds) in the SOW appendix. We can include a separate one-time onboarding credit ($45k) instead of the percentage-based bridge if that’s what Exec prefers — call it out and we’ll swap the line items.

If HelioCharge confirms Option A with onboarding credit substitution, we’ll prepare the DocuSign-ready SOW + PO appendix and push to billing to schedule invoice on 2028-07-01.

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v2_HelioCharge.pdf (SOW v2), pricing_workbook_optionA_B.xlsx (pricing workbook)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Priya Singh <procurement@heliocharge.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Liu <ben@heliocharge.com>, Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@heliocharge.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: commit recalibration + invoice timing

Thanks Marissa — that’s helpful. A few clarifying points from finance and the Exec team:

1) Invoice timing: moving the first invoice to 2028-07-01 works if Redwood can hold revenue recognition until that date on your side (we need the invoice to align with our FY). Please confirm with finance/legal.

2) SLA credits: our legal team wants explicit credit formulas for availability < 99.5% and latency > 2x baseline. Can we add a short appendix with exact math (examples) so our counsel can sign off quickly?

3) Onboarding credit vs percent bridge: Exec likes the one-time onboarding credit but asks that it be payable against milestone: 50% credited after successful migration baseline (30 days) and 50% at full rollout (90 days).

If you can send a DocuSign version with the onboarding credit milestone language and explicit SLA formulas, we can take to CFO next week.

Best,
Priya

> Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Attached is a short worksheet and an updated SOW (v2) that implements...
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: Priya Singh <procurement@heliocharge.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, billing@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 16:04:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Renewal negotiation: commit recalibration + invoice timing

Priya —

Thanks for the quick feedback and the milestone preference — makes sense. To confirm and keep momentum:

- Final deal structure (what we will put into the SOW/PO): 12-mo commit; price-hold for first 6 months; one-time onboarding credit $45,000 paid as: 50% after migration baseline (30 days), 50% at full rollout (90 days). Bridge % removed in favor of the onboarding credit.
- Invoice: Redwood billing will issue the first renewal invoice dated 2028-07-01 to match HelioCharge FY start. Billing (cc’d) — please schedule and confirm revenue recognition implications with finance.
- SLA appendix: we will add explicit formulas and a handful of examples (availability < 99.5% => credit = 5% of monthly invoice per incident capped at 50% monthly; latency regressions defined relative to a 95th percentile baseline). Karthik, please add the legal-friendly language; Marissa will attach the updated SOW v2 and DocuSign envelope.
- Timeline: we’ll aim to have DocuSign sent by Mon 2028-03-05 so HelioCharge can route to CFO the following week.

Action items:
- Marissa: update SOW/DocuSign with milestone onboarding credit and SLA formulas (due Mon 2028-03-05).
- Karthik: confirm invoice / revenue recognition note for billing (reply here).
- Billing: prepare first renewal invoice to be issued with an invoice date of 2028-07-01 pending signed DocuSign.

Priya — once the DocuSign is out we’ll share the HubSpot deal link (copied below) and the DocuSign prep link so you have everything for your CFO. Appreciate the collaboration — let me know if Exec wants any alternate milestone timing.

Thanks,
Grace O’Connor
